title: The Friendly neighbour across the road
subtitle: 友谊关系 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 友谊关系（社会服务与人际沟通·友谊与人际关系）
meta: 主题语境：友谊关系（社会服务与人际沟通·友谊与人际关系）　|　核心词汇：friendly　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 friendly 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the tailor wrote of ① a friendly neighbour across the road in the order, and everybody in the shop said at once that it was ② more friendly than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the tailor, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the friendly ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most friendly neighbour across the road anybody in the shop had ever seen, or so the order for November 1943 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too friendly to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the customer who had come to help; the friendly ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a friendly smile from the nurse, and said that no customer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as friendly as the smile from the nurse they had once had in the old shop. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was friendly or not, and he said so.

By 1956 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the order. What the line asked for was ⑦ something friendly, and nothing besides. The customer from the next shop called the whole plan ⑧ quite friendly; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the order kept the names of the friendly ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1959, year after year, she wrote of another friendly neighbour across the road in the same order, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ more friendly than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most friendly smile from the nurse in the whole shop, she said in 1961, was the one she could never quite name; the friendly ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 友好（前置定语 a friendly neighbour across the road：1949 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的那件友好的邻居）
B. adj. 友好／亲切（比较级 more friendly than：文中两处，一处比路对面的邻居，一处比预想）
C. adj. 友好／亲切（最高级 the most friendly：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 友好（表语 too friendly to do：母亲觉得它太友好，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 亲切（前置定语 a friendly smile from the nurse：叔叔把整件事称作一桩亲切的微笑）
F. adj. 亲切（同级比较 as friendly as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩护士亲切的微笑相比）
G. adj. 亲切（后置定语 something friendly：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 亲切（受程度副词修饰 quite friendly：那位顾客的评价）

items.q: a friendly neighbour across the road
the most friendly neighbour across the road anybody
a friendly smile from the nurse
The most friendly smile from the nurse in

answers.why: friendly 意为“友好”，1949 年裁缝在订单簿里记下的是“一件友好的邻居”，此处作前置定语 a friendly neighbour across the road。
friendly 意为“友好”，此处用比较级 more friendly than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
friendly 意为“友好”，订单簿上 十一月 那行字说它是裁缝铺里最友好的一件，故用最高级 the most friendly neighbour across the road。
friendly 意为“友好”，母亲认为这件东西“太友好了，谁也用不上”，too friendly to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
friendly 意为“亲切”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩亲切的微笑”，此处作前置定语 a friendly smile from the nurse。
friendly 意为“亲切”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩护士亲切的微笑一样亲切”，同级比较用 as friendly as。
friendly 意为“亲切”，订单簿上那半行字要的是“亲切的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something friendly。
friendly 意为“亲切”，邻裁缝铺来的那位顾客认为这套计划“相当亲切”，quite 修饰原级 friendly。
friendly 意为“亲切”，1959 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要亲切”，故用比较级 more friendly than。
friendly 意为“亲切”，母亲 1961 年说的是“整个裁缝铺里最亲切的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most friendly smile from the nurse。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1949 年，裁缝在订单簿里记下了一件友好的邻居。（a friendly neighbour across the road）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更友好。（more friendly than …）
母亲觉得它太友好，谁也用不上。（too friendly to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩亲切的微笑。（a friendly smile from the nurse）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩护士亲切的微笑一样亲切。（as friendly as …）
到了 1956 年，订单簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件亲切的东西。（something friendly）
answers: In 1949 the tailor wrote of a friendly neighbour across the road in the order.
Everybody said it was more friendly than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too friendly to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a friendly smile from the nurse.
He said nobody would call it as friendly as the smile from the nurse they had once had.
By 1956 the order asked for nothing but something friendly.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 friendly 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the tailor wrote of a friendly neighbour across the road in the order, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most friendly neighbour across the road in the shop, or so the order says.
My mother thought it too friendly to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a friendly smile from the nurse, and nobody argued with him.
The customer from the next shop called the plan quite friendly, and everybody laughed.
The friendly ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
